Comment: Permissions required by the human (or CI principal) who DEPLOYS the XamOps
CloudFormation stacks. This is not granted to XamOps and is not part of any stack —
it is what the deploying identity needs in order to create the resources.
Derived from every resource type used across xamops-cur-report.yml,
xamops-mpa-cur-role.yml, the readonly/readwrite role templates and the nested
inventory-events template.
Note the read actions (Get*, Describe*, List*). CloudFormation calls them during
create AND during rollback, and its newer pre-deployment validation calls them to
check whether a resource already exists. Missing a read action fails the stack just
as hard as missing a write one, and additionally breaks rollback — which is how a
stack ends up stuck in ROLLBACK_FAILED with orphaned resources.
cur:* rather than an enumerated list. The whole cur service is six actions, all of
them about report definitions, and CloudFormation calls several of them during a
single create — PutReportDefinition, then DescribeReportDefinitions and
ListTagsForResource to read the resource back. Enumerating them is how the
ListTagsForResource failure happened in the first place.
Resource must be * : cur:DescribeReportDefinitions is a list operation and does not
accept a resource ARN.
Scoped by RESOURCE rather than by action, deliberately.
The AWS::S3::Bucket handler reads back every sub-resource after creating a bucket —
versioning, logging, notifications, CORS, replication, ownership controls, object
lock, intelligent tiering, analytics, metrics, inventory — even though this template
sets none of them. Enumerating those ~20 Get* actions correctly is guesswork, and
each one missed is another failed stack plus a broken rollback.
s3:* confined to the xamops-cur-* buckets is both more reliable AND tighter than a
long action list on Resource "*": it cannot touch any other bucket in the account,
whereas the enumerated version could have edited the policy of every one of them.
Account-level operations that cannot be scoped to a bucket ARN.
